newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Cemex seeks lion's share of Colombian market.
newsitem.headline: Cemex seeks lion's share of Colombian market.

text.p: Mexican cement giant Cementos Mexicanos will invest $190 million in Colombia over the next two years to help consolidate its position as a dominant player in the Andean nation's cement market, a company official said.

Juan Romero, the head of all Cemex operations in Colombia, told reporters Wednesday night that the investment would boost the production capacity of its two Colombian subsidiaries to a total of 5 million metric tons a year, up from a current capacity of 3.4 million metric tons.

According to Romero, Colombia's internal demand for cement is currently about 7.7 million metric tons per year, so the projected boost in production capacity would theoretically allow Cemex to corner the market.

Cemex spent an estimated $700 million this year to purchase controlling stakes in Colombia's Cementos Diamante and Industrias e Inversiones Samper, two of the country's largest independent cement makers.

The Colombian market has been hard hit by a projected 10 percent drop in the construction industry this year. But industry analysts say it has enormous potential for growth because of the country's crumbling public infrastructure and a projected surge in oil export revenues next year.

The analysts say Cemex will face stiff competition in Colombia from the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group, which owns five leading cement manufacturers and currently controls about half of the market.
